subject: Redwood Private - Disconnected Infrastructure Capabilities (RFI)
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@harbingerhealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@harbingerhealth.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Disconnected deployment questionnaire for Harbinger Health

Dylan —

Thanks for taking the call earlier. As part of our procurement process we need a written response to a short set of questions around running Redwood Private in a fully disconnected environment (no outbound internet from the inference cluster). Key items we care about: offline installation, patching cadence & delivery, certificate management, SBOM and supply-chain attestations, telemetry (what can remain offline), and how licensing/activation works without internet.

I've attached the RFI PDF (harbinger_rfi_v1_questions.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can:

- Accept air-gapped installs with manual bundle application by our infra team?
- Support KMS/HSM integrations for model keys and not exfiltrate any model artifacts?
- Ship a signed SBOM and attestations we can log for audit?
- Provide a deterministic offline upgrade bundle and rollback instructions?

We're on a tight schedule for vendor submissions — target close is next Wednesday.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
CISO, Harbinger Health
elena.ruiz@harbingerhealth.com

Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask and the RFI. Short answer: yes on all four bullets with some implementation notes. I'm attaching our offline install playbook and SBOM extract for audit. Below is a concise summary you can use in the RFP response; I'll follow up with Marissa and Markus for any detailed artifacts you need.

Summary answers (high level)
- Offline installation: Supported. We provide a signed, checksummed installation bundle (tar + manifest + detached signature). Customer ops can copy the bundle into the isolated environment and run the installer. No outbound connectivity is required.
- Patching & upgrades: Deterministic offline upgrade bundles published per release. Each bundle includes a pre/post checklist, a migration plan, and an automated rollback script. We support both fast-path patch bundles (hot patches for CVEs) and full-version upgrades.
- Certificates & secrets: Redwood Private supports customer-provided TLS certs and can integrate with on-prem HSMs or KMIP-compatible KMS. Keys and model artifacts remain on the customer network; we do not persist secrets outside the cluster unless explicitly configured for managed backups.
- SBOM & attestations: We publish signed SBOMs in SPDX and CSV formats and provide a signed attestation package (sha256-signed) suitable for SOC/audit ingestion.

I'll call out a couple of things we often clarify in RFPs:
- Telemetry: By default, telemetry is disabled in air-gapped installs. If you want periodic metrics, we provide an export bundle (encrypted) that you can move via jump-box to a pull endpoint; alternatively we can provide a manual CSV export run book.
- License activation: Offline license activation is supported via time-limited activation tokens in the install bundle or via a signed license file you drop into the cluster. We also support an offline HSM-binding step to tie the license to hardware.

Attachments: redwood_offline_install_playbook_v1.3.pdf, redwood_signed_sbom_20270414.csv

Next steps: if the above looks good I can populate the RFI PDF with more granular answers and proposed verification steps (e.g., a dry-run install checklist and acceptance criteria). Can you confirm the required format for submission (PDF vs. XLS) and whether Harbinger needs an on-site install window?

Thanks,

Thanks, that summary helps. For the formal submission we need a populated PDF and a short install acceptance checklist (one page) that we can show the audit team. Harbinger cannot permit vendor personnel on site for installs — our infra will run the bundle and validation checks remotely.

Two clarifying Qs:
1) Will the install bundle validate host-level preconditions (e.g., kernel params, firewall, ulimit) and fail with an error report if checks don't pass?
2) For cryptographic verification of bundles, do you provide a public GPG/PKI key we can pin in our provisioning pipeline?

Elena

On a related note, can you also confirm any telemetry we would be asked to enable during a pilot? We need to ensure nothing leaves our network during that period.
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Elena —

Answering your technical clarification items below. I'm Markus (on our infra/security engineering team) — copied Marissa for product/commercial context.

1) Preflight checks and host validation:
- Yes — installers include a preflight validator that checks kernel versions, required cgroups, sysctl settings, iptables/nftables reachability (ports can be configured), SELinux/AppArmor mode, disk layout, and ulimit. The validator produces a machine-readable JSON report and a human-friendly summary. If a hard precondition fails, the installer aborts and writes a diagnostics bundle you can share for remote triage.

2) Cryptographic verification and pinning: 
- We publish a long-lived vendor signing key (RSA-4096) and rotate it on a predictable cadence. Each bundle includes a detached signature and a manifest with sha256 checksums. Harbinger can pin either the vendor public key or a specific bundle fingerprint in your provisioning system. We can also support an option where you generate a customer keypair and we sign the bundle with a customer-provided signing key during purchase.

Telemetry during pilot:
- Telemetry is opt-in for pilots. The default pilot configuration is zero egress. If your pilot needs metrics, we provide an encrypted metrics export archive that your ops team can copy out via an approved jump host. We also document the exact metric names and buckets so you can run local assertions without exporting data.

I'll attach the preflight checklist snippet and a short acceptance checklist as an HTML snippet in the populated RFI.

Regards,
Markus Klein
